framework.caption: Controlled normal-reference framework. (a) The K verified normal images of one category pass through the same frozen branches, are mapped to the common grid and normalized branch by branch, and build a fixed reference bank whose rows keep one identity across branches; the query never writes to the bank. (b) A query image follows the same frozen path and is scored against that bank under one matching rule. The two task paths use different background shades. The extra slot holds S (DINOv2-S) or D (WideResNet50-2) in the controlled constructions only, so it is an experimental configuration rather than a runtime switch, and DUP trains no new model. The lower-right panels show one real MPDD query (metal_plate/test/scratches/026.png, seed 0, K = 1) with its dual-branch A1 score map and a contour derived from that same map: the map is min-max quantized to 256 levels and thresholded by Otsu for visualization only, no ground-truth mask is loaded to extract the contour, and the rule is not a calibrated deployment threshold. Patch scores are resized to the retained canvas and smoothed with a Gaussian of standard deviation 4; the image score is the spatial maximum. B is DINOv2-B, C the AnomalyCLIP visual path.

matching.caption: Joint and independent matching on the same fixed bank. (a) One query patch and the candidate reference rows r = 1, ..., 8; the shaded cell in each branch row marks the candidate that branch finds closest. The cells are ordering indicators only and carry no measured value. (b) J requires a single shared reference row for all branches and then minimizes the weighted sum of distances over candidates, whereas L lets each branch take its own nearest row before the weighted sum is formed. Both panels use the same aligned candidate set, the same branch descriptors and the same nonnegative weights that sum to one, so the two panels differ only in the order of combination and candidate minimization.

constructions.caption: Fixed representation constructions and the contrasts built from them. (a) A1, DUP, TRI and BAL with their distance weights; a slot keeps the same colour across panels. (b) A1 to DUP varies only the effective weight of B and is therefore the weight-confounding control; DUP to TRI puts a real encoder into the slot at an unchanged weight; A1 to BAL keeps the non-C family total and the C weight equal. (c) The four contrasts estimated in this paper. The TRI-to-A1 difference moves both factors at once and is never attributed to S alone. The extra slot is instantiated by five frozen encoders: S and D were pre-specified, while E1, E2 and E3 were added after the S and D results were known and are exploratory transfer checks. These are analysis configurations in one frozen pipeline, not trained networks.

effects.caption: Observed representation effects and their matching interactions, with paired percentile intervals on stride-eight pixels. (a) Representation swap E = P(new) - P(control) with unadjusted 95% intervals, for S = DINOv2-S on the 12 MPDD and 8 BTAD support conditions and for the prespecified D = WideResNet50-2 branch on the restricted scope of seeds 0 and 1 with K = 1 and 4. (b) The direct interactions I = E_L - E_J, one row per dataset and contrast and one lane per encoder: the S and D lanes are pre-specified, the E1, E2 and E3 lanes were added later and are exploratory, and the MVTec AD and VisA rows, drawn as a single lane, come from the four-dataset generalization table of Section 4.2.10. Every interval drawn here is the unadjusted 95% paired interval; the family-adjusted intervals are reported in Sections 4.2.4, 4.2.10 and 4.2.11. The support scopes of the S series, the D series, the extra encoders and the MVTec AD/VisA rows are not identical, and Section 4.2.11 records that the E1 to E3 lanes pool twelve support conditions while the S and D lanes and the primary five-encoder rows use four; the vertical distance between lanes of different scope is therefore not an encoder effect.

budget_category.caption: Interaction against the nested support budget, across categories and across seeds. (a) Seed-averaged stride-eight point estimates of I_TRI and I_BAL against K. K = 2, 4 and 8 are nested prefixes of the same support sequence, so the four budgets are not independent samples, and the lines connect evaluated budgets without implying a fitted trend. (b) I_TRI per category on the MPDD study revision and the BTAD corrected revision. Bracket_white and connector carry the widest intervals, so the MPDD average is not produced by one narrow estimate. (c) The same two interactions per seed over seeds 0 to 7: seeds 0 to 2 use their own query block and seeds 3 to 7 share one resampling block, so the latter measure support-set variation alone. The eight-seed batch is descriptive only, and its reproduction gate passes at the dataset macro level (Section 4.2.11), so panel (c) can be read beside the aggregate tables. These per-budget, per-category and per-seed values are exploratory follow-up analyses that do not inherit the multiplicity adjustment of the primary family.

cases_good.caption: Three selected MPDD improvements for A1 L relative to A1 J at seed 0 and K = 4. Values are stored stride-eight per-image AP, rather than the category-pooled AP used in the main tables. J/L heatmaps share one full-map min-max range per row. The cyan L contour uses 256-bin Otsu thresholding on that normalized score. Red hollow rectangles define identical GT-centered visual crops, enlarged below. GT is used for evaluation and crop placement, never to generate the predicted contour. These are selected extremes, not a random test sample.
cases_good.continuation_caption: Figure 6 continued. The third selected improvement, with the same scale, crop, and contour conventions.

cases_bad.caption: Two selected MPDD degradations under the same A1 comparison and display protocol as Figure 6. Lower raw scores under independent matching do not guarantee improved pixel ordering or a complete contour. The cases illustrate matching behaviour at the anchor and are not direct evidence of the representation interaction. A companion per-sample comparison set, generated from the same common valid region as Table 11, places selected samples beside the native baselines at seed 0 with K = 4: MPDD (six method columns, six categories), BTAD (six, three), MVTec AD (six, fifteen) and VisA (six, twelve). Each class shows the three test images with the largest spread of per-sample pixel AP, the panels of a row share one colour scale, and in the current set every method column carries data for every displayed unit; a column whose per-sample dump did not cover a unit would be retained as n/a rather than dropped. The set is archived with the figure sources.

resources.caption: Recorded per-unit cost on the single archived machine. (a) Peak process GPU memory in MB; the PatchCore row is empty because the per-process query returned N/A on this machine and no device-wide substitute is used. (b) Peak process RAM in MB; the controlled A1 configuration has no recorded field, so it is absent rather than estimated. (c) Stage time per unit, where one unit is one dataset, seed and K; PatchCore reports its bank and scoring stages as a single combined total because the vendored interface does not separate them. These are partially instrumented stage measurements, not a synchronized end-to-end latency, and A1 has no comparable complete historical timing.

encoders_geo.label: S1
encoders_geo.caption: Frozen branches and their native geometry. (a) The four branch instances of the controlled matrix with their source weights, input geometry, native patch grid and retained descriptor width. Both DINOv2 branches use a 14-pixel patch and already sit on the common grid; the C branch is resampled from its own grid, and the D branch concatenates layer2 and layer3 on the B canvas. (b) Every branch is mapped to the B canvas by a bilinear resample with align_corners = False and then unit-normalized per position, so the distance actually used is one minus the cosine similarity. (c) What is frozen, how wide the fused vector is, and the three exploratory extra branches: E1 (deiT-small/8, 384 dimensions), E2 (ConvNeXt-Tiny, 576) and E3 (Swin-Tiny, 576) were added after the S and D results were known, giving fused widths of 1536 for A1, 2304 for DUP, 1920 for TRI with S or E1, 3072 for D and 2112 for E2 or E3. No target-domain training, dimensionality reduction, coreset or foreground selection is applied, the fusion weights are fixed by the protocol and never searched, and the C branch contributes only its visual path, with no text or prompt score entering the anomaly score.

shared_op_ablation.label: S2
shared_op_ablation.caption: The one completed ablation of a shared operation. (a) The interaction I = E_L - E_J under each ablation, with the per-category values drawn as circles behind each mean. (b) The absolute mean pixel AP that the same ablations move, over the four constructions under the joint rule. The operations every construction shares are removed one at a time: ABL-S drops the Gaussian smoothing of the patch scores, ABL-N drops the per-branch normalization and scores with squared Euclidean distance, and ABL-C replaces score-level fusion with naive concatenation, which can move only the BAL contrast because the coefficients equal the weights for equal slots. The scope is a single condition, seed 0 with K = 1, and one run per ablation, so no interval exists and none is drawn; the panel is therefore exploratory and does not show that a shared operation has been validated.

extra_cases.label: S3
extra_cases.continuation_caption: Figure S3 continued. The same material as full-width picture panels: the coordinate-region shift of the one non-square audited unit, the canvas coverage, and the eight per-image cases of the frozen selection rule, the last of which is paginated over two pages.
extra_cases.caption: Supporting panels for the geometry audit and the per-image cases. (a) The coordinate shift of the only non-square audited unit, BTAD category 03, together with three units whose shift is zero (mpdd/bracket_black, btad/01 and mpdd/tubes). (b) The eight per-image cases of the frozen case-selection rule, each labelled with its interaction role and value. The companion page reproduces the same material at full panel width, including the per-image case grid over two pages, so that every label stays legible at the manuscript's figure width. These panels document the geometry audit and the case selection; they are not additional evidence for the interaction.
